body.statement: In the six-unit construction, any completion with the missing outcome below \(1\) gives supported rank sums \((9,8,13,12)\) and upper tail \(3/4\), whereas any completion strictly between \(1\) and \(2\) gives \((9,9,12,12)\) and upper tail \(1\). Thus an interior completion strictly dominates the lower extreme even though both completions have no outcome ties.
body.justification: The witness isolates why exchangeable extreme-imputation logic fails under a covariate-constrained support.
body.gap: The extreme-completion simplification of Li, Sheng, and Yu uses an exchangeable assignment law and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. This support is uniform and complement-symmetric but balance-restricted, and ordinary midranks make an interior completion optimal.
body.consumer: It gives a regression test for any implementation and prevents an invalid endpoint-only optimizer.
